A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Vlearn research despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on five Gymnasium tasks and three DMC dog tasks, plus Humanoid component and replay-buffer ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original MyoHand evaluations and component ablations on additional Gymnasium tasks.

M1.justification: The weighted Bellman-error objective, TRPL policy update, twin critics, importance-weight clipping and replay-buffer procedure remain unchanged. Renaming the loss to LWIS and moving the unchanged Algorithm 1 to Appendix B do not change the method.

E1.justification: v3 adds ten 39-dimensional MyoHand tasks from MyoSuite, covering pose, reaching and object manipulation with standard and hard variants (Figure 3). This substantially extends coverage beyond locomotion; all five Gymnasium and three DMC dog tasks remain.

E2.justification: The retained benchmark comparisons still evaluate SAC, MPO, PPO, on-policy TRPL and one-step V-trace, and the component variants remain the same. The new MyoHand comparison uses existing comparators SAC, PPO, TRPL and V-trace; Figure 3 does not report MPO results.

E3.justification: v3 introduces success-based MyoHand evaluation and cross-task IQM aggregation (Figure 3), supplementing the existing per-task return evaluations. Settings for the retained tasks in Tables 1–2 and the controlled one-step V-trace comparison remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Component ablations expand from Humanoid-v4 alone to Ant-v4 and, in Appendix C Figure 6, Hopper-v4, Walker2D-v4 and HalfCheetah-v4. These substantially broaden the investigation of whether importance sampling, TRPL, twin critics and clipping are beneficial across tasks.

E5.justification: v3 adds an interquartile-mean estimate with a 95% bootstrapped confidence interval across MyoHand tasks (Figure 3). Per-task reporting continues to use ten seeds, means and 95% bootstrapped intervals; no increase in runs for retained results is stated.

E6.justification: v3 adds MyoHand success curves showing Vlearn's highest aggregate performance with task-specific exceptions, plus results from the expanded component ablations. Figure 6 also shows that removing twin critics improves HalfCheetah performance. The retained benchmark curves and the reported 25% Humanoid improvement over SAC are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, the upper-bound and consistency proofs, and the bandit variance/effective-sample-size analysis in Appendix A remain mathematically unchanged. Loss renaming, notation corrections and expanded explanations introduce no new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract changes from introducing a novel importance-sampling loss to using an existing weighted loss, and removes the exploration/exploitation claim. The introduction emphasizes feasibility and practical design insights while retaining the central state-value-only learning and high-dimensional-control claims.

C2.justification: v3 extends the twin-critic regularization interpretation by suggesting greater benefits in higher-dimensional problems, and discusses overactuated systems and categorical critics as future directions. The HalfCheetah weakness remains in Section 4.3, although the conclusion no longer repeats it.

D1.justification: Table 2 now explicitly documents the hyperparameters for MyoHand by sharing the dog-task configuration. Existing algorithm details, hyperparameter values, hardware and training-time disclosures remain; the new reproducibility statement mainly directs readers to this material.

R1.justification: v3 expands the connection to prior linear WIS and TD(0) work and clarifies attribution. It adds references for MyoSuite, double sampling, Sutton and Barto's textbook, and recent critic/stabilization approaches, while retaining the overall positioning against Q-function methods and V-trace.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes the narrative around high-dimensional control, expands the WIS explanation and restructures experiments into high-dimensional tasks, design choices and low-dimensional tasks. It also retitles the paper, moves pseudocode into the appendix, adds a reproducibility section and removes the broader-impacts appendix.

P2.justification: Existing Gymnasium and dog plots are regrouped into Figures 2 and 5; a new MyoHand Figure 3 and appendix ablation Figure 6 are added. Figure 4 becomes a wider three-panel comparison, and the algorithm moves from a wrapped main-text display to a full-width appendix display.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens support for the central generality claim: v2 evaluated locomotion and examined components only on Humanoid, whereas v3 adds musculoskeletal hand control and checks component effects across all five Gymnasium tasks. The new results expose task-dependent exceptions, while clearer attribution distinguishes the existing WIS foundation from the practical algorithm contribution. These changes materially improve validation and scientific clarity.
